name: blender boolean bracket with cylinder holes
goal: Model a simple mm bracket plate and cut bolt holes with cylinder Boolean Difference.

source.title: How to 3D Model Using Blender - Easy Beginner Guide + Tips and Tricks

inputs.name: bolt_hole_mm
inputs.description: Hole diameter with clearance (e.g. 5.6 for 5mm bolt)

outputs.name: bracket_mesh
outputs.description: Plate with boolean-cut holes; optional L-flange via extrude

constraints: Cutter cylinders should be taller than plate thickness to avoid coplanar glitches
Increase cylinder vertices (e.g. 256) before confirming add for rounder printed holes
Boolean Difference then Apply; delete cutters afterward

steps.action: Optional: delete Camera and Light (right-click Delete) to declutter.
Set cube dimensions for the plate (e.g. 100 mm wide, 12 deep, 3 thick); rename to bracket.
Add → Mesh → Cylinder; before confirming, open Add Cylinder panel and raise Vertices (e.g. 256).
Size cutter diameter with clearance (e.g. 5.6 mm) and height taller than plate (e.g. 10 mm); rename hole cutter.
Duplicate cutters, position along plate (set Location numerically); Shift-select cutters → Join into one cutter object.
Select bracket → Modifiers → Add Boolean → Object = hole cutter, Operation Difference → Apply.
Delete cutter object(s); verify holes. Tab Edit mode; Face select; E extrude an edge/face to form an L-bracket flange as needed.
Optional: enable MeasureIt add-on (Edit→Preferences→Add-ons) to measure hole diameters in mm.

verification: Boolean applied (modifier not still live unless intentional)
